practiceNotes: Spaced recall maintains definitions, representations, assumptions and method selection. Proofs, programming, experiments and extended judgments require separately assessed performance.
Use unfamiliar transfer problems, delayed reassessment, alternative representations and error diagnosis; memorized worked examples are insufficient evidence of competence.
Implementation assessments require executable tests, reproducible environments and independent validation. Using a provided solver or library does not establish implementation or proof competence.
Laboratory assessments require appropriate facilities, instrument induction and supervision. Supplied or simulated data can assess inference but cannot certify hands-on technique.
Human, animal, microbial, genetic and environmental work requires applicable consent, ethics review, containment and authorization; these conditions are not assumed satisfied.
Security exercises require explicitly authorized isolated systems. Radiation, lasers, high voltage, pressure systems and hazardous chemistry require qualified supervision.
Physical robot deployment, clinical practice, environmental release and regulated industrial operations require separate safety assessment and professional authorization.
Extended projects should preserve raw evidence, uncertainty calculations, negative results and justified accessibility, welfare, environmental and stakeholder decisions.

Interpret motion graphs and calculate constant-acceleration trajectories in one and two dimensions.

decks.title: Ecology
decks.description: Explain ecological patterns with models and field evidence.

includes: Demography, interactions, ecosystems, nutrient cycles and field sampling

practice: Audit field data and compare demographic and interaction explanations for an abundance pattern.

outcomes.description: Represent competition, predation, mutualism, succession, food webs and carbon, nitrogen and energy budgets.
Design quadrat, transect and mark-recapture studies; estimate abundance and diversity and assess detection and spatial confounding.
Calculate discrete projections, life-table reproduction and bounded exponential or logistic growth with explicit density and closure assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Experimentation
decks.description: Generate controlled biological evidence.

includes: Microscopy, volumetry, asepsis, bounded DNA assays, design and ethics

practice: Conduct a safe microscopy or DNA-assay study with controls, an analysis plan and ethical alternatives.

outcomes.description: Specify biological and technical replication, randomization, blinding and endpoints; analyze effects with descriptive and resampling procedures.
Compare study alternatives using welfare, consent, biosafety, stewardship, environmental impact and evidential value.
Calibrate microscopy and pipetting; explain asepsis, DNA extraction, template copying in PCR and size separation in gels; execute controlled protocols.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genetics
decks.description: Infer inheritance from crosses and families.

includes: Meiosis, inheritance, linkage, pedigrees and genetic variation

practice: Compare genetic models for a new pedigree and design a discriminating cross.

outcomes.description: Relate chromosomes and meiosis to Mendelian, sex-linked, cytoplasmic and non-Mendelian inheritance; calculate cross and pedigree probabilities.
Infer linkage order and recombination distances; distinguish complementation, epistasis and allelism through experiments.
Interpret mutation, chromosome variation, penetrance, expressivity and genotype-environment effects without genetic determinism.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Atomic Structure and Bonding
decks.description: Predict qualitative molecular structure and properties.

includes: Orbitals, periodicity, bonding diagrams, geometry and intermolecular forces

practice: Compare bonding explanations for unfamiliar molecules and defend property predictions.

outcomes.description: Assign electron configurations and explain spectra and periodic trends through quantized shells and orbital representations.
Construct Lewis, resonance, VSEPR, hybridization and qualitative molecular-orbital diagrams; predict geometry, bond order, polarity and magnetism.
Relate intermolecular forces and bonding types to solubility, phase behavior and material properties; identify model limitations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Equilibria and Electrochemistry
decks.description: Calculate equilibrium chemical responses.

includes: Mass action, aqueous speciation, redox and electrochemical cells

practice: Predict a mixed solution's titration and precipitation and verify conservation for every species.

outcomes.description: Calculate buffers, titration curves, solubility and coupled speciation using mass and charge balances and checked approximations.
Construct quotients and balances; use explicitly explained Gibbs-energy and equilibrium-constant relations under ideal assumptions.
Balance redox reactions; calculate Nernst potentials and electrolysis quantities and distinguish thermodynamic favorability from kinetics.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Kinetics
decks.description: Infer rates and discriminate mechanisms.

includes: Rate laws, mechanisms, steady-state approximations, catalysis and temperature effects

practice: Fit candidate laws by explicit parameter scans and design a mechanism-discriminating experiment.

outcomes.description: Construct elementary-step equations and derive pre-equilibrium and steady-state approximations for consecutive, parallel and catalytic pathways.
Infer and derive zero-, first- and second-order laws; estimate parameters from initial-rate and time-course data with residual checks.
Estimate Arrhenius parameters and distinguish activation, equilibrium, mixing and temperature-control effects.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Laboratory Practice
decks.description: Perform reliable basic chemical operations.

includes: Preparation, separation, wet assays, records, uncertainty and safety judgment

practice: Prepare and assay an unknown, close mass balance and defend separation and waste procedures.

outcomes.description: Execute standardized titration and gravimetric assays using explained indicator chemistry; calculate blanks, calibration, recovery and uncertainty.
Maintain traceable records and justify alternatives using hazard, exposure, incompatibility, waste and reproducibility evidence.
Perform weighing, volumetry, filtration, extraction and distillation with recovery and contamination controls.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
decks.description: Design efficient algorithms with guarantees.

includes: Data structures, graph algorithms, dynamic programming, flows and complexity analysis

practice: Implement routing and allocation algorithms, prove guarantees and benchmark adversarial inputs.

outcomes.description: Prove correctness with invariants and induction; derive worst-case, expected and amortized time-space bounds, defining needed expectation models.
Implement sorting, traversal, shortest paths, spanning trees, greedy methods and dynamic programming with explicit states and recurrences.
Implement augmenting-path maximum flow and bipartite matching; prove max-flow/min-cut and reduction correctness.
Implement arrays, linked structures, hash tables, heaps, balanced search trees and disjoint sets.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Applied Learning Foundations
decks.description: Build honest predictive baselines without advanced theory.

includes: Transparent prediction models, splitting, feature preparation and evaluation

practice: Implement baseline predictors and perform a leakage, calibration and subgroup audit on unfamiliar data.

outcomes.description: Separate training, validation and testing; fit preprocessing only on training data and assess confusion, calibration, subgroup errors and deployment consequences.
Implement nearest neighbors, finite naive Bayes and greedy decision trees from explicit distance, smoothing and impurity formulas.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Architecture
decks.description: Explain execution on digital hardware.

includes: Digital logic, number representation, instructions, pipelines and memory hierarchy

practice: Build a CPU emulator and compare cache traces for equivalent computations.

outcomes.description: Construct combinational and sequential circuits and controllers; represent signed integers and floating-point arithmetic.
Trace assembly, calling conventions and pipelines; implement a small instruction-set emulator and diagnose hazards.
Analyze pointers, memory layout, caches and locality; predict access-pattern performance.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Database Systems
decks.description: Design and query reliable persistent data.

includes: Relational modeling, SQL, normalization, indexes, transactions and recovery

practice: Build a reservation database and test conflicting bookings, rollback and indexed plans.

outcomes.description: Construct relational schemas from entities and dependencies; use keys and normalization to prevent anomalies.
Write joins, aggregation and nested SQL; explain relational algebra, B-tree and hash indexing and query plans.
Analyze isolation, locking and transaction schedules; implement integrity tests and explain write-ahead recovery.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction
decks.description: Design systems around human capabilities and obligations.

includes: Task analysis, accessible interaction, prototyping, user studies and judgment

practice: Evaluate alternative prototypes in an approved study and revise using accessibility and privacy evidence.

outcomes.description: Plan usability studies and analyze task completion, errors and qualitative evidence with appropriate uncertainty.
Analyze tasks and create accessible interaction flows using feedback, consistency, error recovery and cognitive-load principles.
Justify decisions involving disability, privacy, consent, manipulation, cultural context and competing stakeholder needs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Languages
decks.description: Define and implement language meaning.

includes: Syntax, semantics, lambda calculus, type systems and interpreters

practice: Implement a specified language and prove type safety for a bounded fragment.

outcomes.description: Implement closures, functions and state in interpreters; compare functional, imperative and object-oriented abstractions.
Specify abstract syntax and operational semantics; compare substitution, environments, evaluation order, lexical scope and mutation.
Construct typing and inference rules; prove representative progress and preservation lemmas by structural induction.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Abstract Algebra
decks.description: Prove algebraic structural relationships.

includes: Groups, actions, rings, ideals, factorization and field extensions

practice: Classify quotient structures and construct a finite field with proved arithmetic.

outcomes.description: Construct finite and simple algebraic extensions; calculate minimal polynomials, extension degrees and bases.
Analyze subgroups, cosets, actions and quotients; prove homomorphism and finite-group structure results.
Construct ideals and quotient rings; prove isomorphism, divisibility and polynomial factorization results.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis
decks.description: Prove validity conditions for limiting arguments.

includes: Completeness, limits, metric spaces, compactness and uniform convergence

practice: Prove a convergence theorem and construct counterexamples to weakened hypotheses.

outcomes.description: Prove differentiation and Riemann-integration results; justify or refute exchanging limits, integrals and derivatives using uniform convergence.
Use completeness, epsilon arguments and subsequences to prove convergence and construct counterexamples.
Prove metric continuity, compactness, connectedness and completeness results, including contraction mapping.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Equations and Dynamics
decks.description: Solve and analyze deterministic evolution.

includes: ODE solutions, linear systems, phase planes, stability and uniqueness

practice: Solve a forced two-state system and compare analytical solutions, phase portraits and numerical steps.

outcomes.description: Formulate initial-value problems; solve separable, first-order linear and forced constant-coefficient second-order equations.
Develop partial-derivative linearization locally; analyze equilibria, phase portraits, uniqueness, bifurcation examples and Euler-step limitations.
Solve linear systems with eigenstructure and matrix exponentials, including repeated eigenvalues and transient modes.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Euclidean Geometry
decks.description: Construct and justify elementary spatial relationships.

includes: Euclidean constructions, congruence, similarity, circles, loci and coordinate proofs

practice: Solve a locus construction synthetically and analytically, checking degenerate cases.

outcomes.description: Construct perpendiculars, bisectors, tangencies and triangle centers with straightedge and compass; justify existence and uniqueness or failure.
Prove unfamiliar triangle, circle and locus claims using congruence, similarity, transformations and coordinate equations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable and Vector Calculus
decks.description: Calculate with multidimensional fields.

includes: Partial derivatives, multiple integrals, coordinate changes and vector integral theorems

practice: Compute three-dimensional mass and flux in two coordinate systems and verify an integral theorem.

outcomes.description: Calculate gradients, Jacobians and Hessians; apply multivariable chain rules, local extrema tests and implicit-function conditions.
Calculate line and surface integrals, divergence and curl; apply Green, Gauss and Stokes theorems with orientation and regularity.
Evaluate multiple integrals in Cartesian, polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates with correct domains and Jacobians.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Elementary Number Theory
decks.description: Prove arithmetic claims without abstract-algebra prerequisites.

includes: Congruences, residues, arithmetic functions, continued fractions and arithmetic algorithms

practice: Solve a Diophantine problem and produce an independently checkable arithmetic certificate.

outcomes.description: Execute modular exponentiation, primality tests and elementary factorization; distinguish probabilistic evidence from verifiable certificates.
Analyze arithmetic functions, continued fractions and elementary Diophantine equations using divisibility, descent and rational approximation.
Prove and apply Euclidean algorithms, Chinese remaindering, multiplicative orders and quadratic reciprocity using elementary arguments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Computation Foundations
decks.description: Implement basic reliable numerical calculations.

includes: Floating-point error, root finding, interpolation, quadrature and linear solvers
excludes: ODE integration and advanced convergence theory

practice: Build tested root and quadrature routines and document conditioning and convergence failures.

outcomes.description: Implement bisection, Newton iteration, interpolation, quadrature and pivoted elimination; explain stopping rules and representative failure cases.
Distinguish conditioning, rounding, truncation and algorithmic stability using residuals, sensitivity and refinement experiments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability
decks.description: Derive consequences of probabilistic models.

includes: Distributions, joint laws, conditioning, moments and classical limits

practice: Derive a transformed measurement distribution and assess an approximation against exact probabilities.

outcomes.description: Calculate joint laws, covariance and conditional expectations using finite sums and explicitly developed iterated density integrals.
Construct discrete and continuous laws, transform random variables and calculate probabilities, expectations and variances.
Apply laws of large numbers, central-limit approximations and elementary concentration inequalities with stated assumptions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Classical Dynamics
decks.description: Derive motion beyond constant acceleration.

includes: Central forces, rotation, noninertial frames and oscillations

practice: Predict coupled oscillations and rotating-body response and compare conservation and mode measurements.

outcomes.description: Derive three-dimensional equations, effective potentials, orbital relations and rotating-frame forces; use conservation to reduce motion.
Solve damped and driven oscillators using taught exponential trial solutions; diagonalize coupled normal-mode systems.
Calculate centers of mass and inertia tensors using developed iterated mass integrals; analyze torque, rolling and gyroscopic motion.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Laboratory Measurement and Electronics
decks.description: Build and assess measurement chains.

includes: Calibration, uncertainty, circuit models, amplifiers, filtering and acquisition

practice: Build a low-voltage sensor chain and report calibration, bandwidth, uncertainty and safe-design reasoning.

outcomes.description: Solve Kirchhoff resistor networks, sinusoidal impedances and RC steps from explicit component equations and exponential models.
Build diode, transistor-switch and op-amp circuits; assess loading, saturation, bandwidth, aliasing and electrical-risk alternatives.
Calibrate sensors and use meters and oscilloscopes; propagate uncertainty using taught sensitivity formulas and distinguish systematic error and noise.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Thermal Physics
decks.description: Predict thermal change and conversion limits.

includes: Thermodynamic laws, engines, phases and elementary heat transport

practice: Analyze calorimetry, cooling and an actual engine against reversible limits.

outcomes.description: Apply temperature, equations of state, internal energy, heat, work and thermodynamic laws with explicit boundaries and signs.
Calculate entropy changes, ideal-gas processes, engine efficiencies and phase-change balances; distinguish state and path quantities.
Calculate steady conduction and radiation; derive and solve lumped cooling by separation, stating coefficient and geometry assumptions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Waves and Optics
decks.description: Predict wave patterns and optical measurements.

includes: Waves, acoustics, ray imaging, interference, diffraction and polarization
excludes: General PDE theory and quantum optics

practice: Design an imaging system and recover wavelength from measured diffraction.

outcomes.description: Calculate interference, gratings, aperture diffraction and polarization intensities; infer wavelength and resolution with measurement uncertainty.
Construct reflection and refraction rays and calculate paraxial image location, magnification and optical-system behavior.
Represent traveling and standing waves; develop partial derivatives locally and derive the one-dimensional string equation and acoustic intensity.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biochemistry and Metabolism
decks.description: Connect molecular interactions to biological function.

includes: Macromolecules, enzyme models, bioenergetics and metabolism

practice: Diagnose enzyme perturbations and construct a metabolic carbon, electron and energy budget.

outcomes.description: Explain Michaelis-Menten and inhibition models; estimate parameters by graphical or grid comparison and assess saturation and model assumptions.
Represent proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates and lipids; explain folding, binding and membrane assembly through chemical interactions.
Track atoms, electrons, ATP and gradients through glycolysis, respiration, photosynthesis and biosynthesis; explain regulation and compartmentation.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolution and Phylogeny
decks.description: Explain change and reconstruct ancestry.

includes: Population change, phylogeny, speciation and macroevolutionary evidence

practice: Reconstruct a small tree and compare selection and drift explanations for population observations.

outcomes.description: Evaluate adaptation, speciation, homology, fossils, extinction and major transitions using comparative and historical evidence.
Construct small parsimony trees and compare finite-state substitution likelihoods through explicitly taught branch probabilities and ancestral-state summation.
Calculate Hardy-Weinberg expectations, selection and migration changes; model drift by binomial sampling and distinguish mechanisms.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry
decks.description: Relate inorganic structure and reactivity.

includes: Main-group chemistry, coordination, ligand fields, solids and organometallic cycles

practice: Infer coordination structures from spectra and magnetism and check a catalytic cycle.

outcomes.description: Represent coordination isomers and ligand fields; calculate d-electron counts and interpret color, magnetism and substitution.
Predict representative main-group structures and reactions using periodicity, acid-base concepts and oxidation states.
Describe unit cells and ionic or network solids; audit electron counts through elementary organometallic catalytic steps.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Symmetry
decks.description: Use symmetry to predict molecular observations.

includes: Point groups, character tables, symmetry-adapted orbitals and normal modes

practice: Assign point groups and predict vibrational observations for unfamiliar molecular geometries.

outcomes.description: Construct symmetry-adapted orbital combinations and vibrational mode representations; predict IR and Raman activity from transformation properties.
Identify symmetry operations and point groups; construct transformation matrices and reduce representations using explained character-table rules.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Structure and Identification
decks.description: Represent and identify small organic molecules.

includes: Organic representations, conformations, stereochemistry and simple IR, NMR and mass spectra

practice: Identify an unknown from combined spectra and defend its three-dimensional representation.

outcomes.description: Assign structures using explained IR frequencies, proton-NMR shifts, integration and first-order splitting, molecular ions and isotope patterns.
Construct wedge-dash, Newman and chair views; assign stereodescriptors and compare enantiomers, diastereomers and conformations.
Translate names, formulas and skeletal structures; distinguish functional groups, constitutional isomers and resonance representations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics
decks.description: Predict nonideal chemical equilibrium.

includes: Potentials, activities, fugacities, mixtures and phase diagrams

practice: Infer a nonideal binary phase diagram and predict temperature-dependent reaction equilibrium.

outcomes.description: Calculate partial molar quantities, activities, fugacities and mixing free energies and temperature-pressure equilibrium dependence.
Construct unary and binary phase diagrams, common tangents, phase-rule constraints and coupled reaction-phase equilibria.
Derive potentials, Maxwell relations and chemical potentials using total differentials and Legendre transformations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Symbolic Artificial Intelligence
decks.description: Solve symbolic reasoning problems.

includes: Search, constraints, logic, adversarial reasoning and planning

practice: Build a planner and compare search, constraint and logical representations.

outcomes.description: Solve constraint problems with propagation, backtracking and variable-order heuristics.
Develop propositional and first-order syntax; implement unification, bounded inference and classical planning with explicit soundness limits.
Implement uninformed, heuristic and adversarial search; prove admissibility-based guarantees in bounded state spaces.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Compiler Construction
decks.description: Translate programs while preserving meaning.

includes: Parsing, semantic analysis, IR, optimization and code generation

practice: Build a compiler with differential tests and measured optimization effects.

outcomes.description: Implement instruction selection, register allocation and calling conventions; validate code against an interpreter.
Implement lexing, recursive-descent and table-driven parsing, symbol resolution and type checking.
Construct control-flow and SSA representations; implement dataflow analysis and semantics-preserving optimizations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Theory of Computation
decks.description: Establish computational expressiveness and limits.

includes: Automata, grammars, computability, reductions and complexity classes

practice: Classify unfamiliar language families and give a complete hardness reduction.

outcomes.description: Classify problems using time and space classes; prove NP-completeness with explicit polynomial reductions and certificates.
Use Turing machines, enumeration, diagonalization and mapping reductions to prove computability or undecidability.
Construct automata, regular expressions, grammars and pushdown machines; prove equivalence and nonexpressibility results.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Graphics and Geometric Vision
decks.description: Construct images and recover geometry.

includes: Geometry, cameras, rasterization, rays, filtering and geometric reconstruction
excludes: Global light transport and learned vision

practice: Build a renderer and reconstruct a tabletop scene against geometric ground truth.

outcomes.description: Represent meshes, homogeneous transformations and cameras; calculate projection, clipping, barycentric interpolation and visibility.
Implement linear camera calibration and two-view triangulation; estimate parameters by least squares and check reprojection and geometric ambiguity.
Implement rasterization and ray intersections with explained local reflectance models; compare finite sampling, convolution filters and aliasing.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Information Theory and Coding
decks.description: Quantify communication limits and construct codes.

includes: Entropy, compression, channel capacity, coding and decoding

practice: Build a compressor and noisy-channel encoder-decoder and compare rates and errors with theoretical bounds.

outcomes.description: Calculate finite-channel capacity and explain typical-sequence achievability; implement linear block codes and syndrome decoding over explicitly taught finite fields.
Derive entropy, mutual information, relative entropy and data-processing inequalities for finite models.
Construct prefix and arithmetic codes; prove Kraft and source-coding bounds and measure compression against entropy.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Networks
decks.description: Implement and diagnose network communication.

includes: Layered protocols, routing, transport, congestion and socket applications

practice: Implement file transfer and diagnose injected loss, delay and malformed messages.

outcomes.description: Trace framing, addressing, checksums, naming and connection establishment across network layers.
Execute link-state and distance-vector routing; analyze retransmission, flow control and congestion under explicit delay-loss models.
Implement framed socket services with timeouts and partial-read handling; capture and diagnose protocol exchanges.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Operating Systems
decks.description: Implement and explain resource management.

includes: Processes, concurrency, memory, scheduling, filesystems, I/O and protection

practice: Build a concurrent storage service and test races, memory pressure and crash recovery.

outcomes.description: Trace virtual address translation, paging and allocation; compare replacement policies and protection boundaries.
Analyze scheduling, races and deadlocks; implement threads, locks and condition-variable synchronization.
Explain filesystem allocation, caching, I/O and crash consistency; implement a bounded storage-layer model.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Quantum Information and Computation
decks.description: Analyze quantum computational constructions and noise.

includes: Finite quantum postulates, qubits, algorithms, channels and error correction
excludes: Continuous wave mechanics and hardware engineering

practice: Implement a quantum algorithm and small error-correcting code, proving ideal guarantees and measuring specified noise effects.

outcomes.description: Implement state-vector amplitude amplification and phase estimation; prove bounded success and query-complexity guarantees.
Develop finite-state normalization, unitary evolution and Born measurement; construct tensor-product circuits, entanglement and teleportation and prove circuit identities.
Develop density matrices, partial traces and channels; calculate noise effects and analyze elementary stabilizer error-correction codes.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Information Retrieval and Language Processing
decks.description: Retrieve and analyze language data.

includes: Indexing, ranking, text processing, statistical language baselines and evaluation

practice: Build a document search engine and text classifier with relevance judgments and error analysis.

outcomes.description: Evaluate ranking with precision, recall and discounted gain and language models with held-out likelihood; audit annotation, multilingual and societal biases.
Implement smoothed n-gram language models and text classification; handle morphology, segmentation and ambiguity with explicit representations.
Implement tokenization, inverted indexes, Boolean retrieval and TF-IDF or explained probabilistic ranking with document-length normalization.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Combinatorics and Graph Theory
decks.description: Prove finite counting and existence results.

includes: Generating functions, extremal graphs, matching and probabilistic existence

practice: Prove an enumeration formula and an extremal existence bound, with small finite checks.

outcomes.description: Derive ordinary and exponential generating functions; use coefficient extraction and recurrences for constrained enumeration.
Prove matching, coloring, connectivity and extremal results; use adjacency matrices to count walks and expose structure.
Use first and second moments and concentration to establish existence and random-structure bounds.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis
decks.description: Use analytic structure for proofs and calculation.

includes: Holomorphic functions, Cauchy theory, residues and conformal maps

practice: Evaluate a parameterized integral and solve a mapped planar boundary problem.

outcomes.description: Test holomorphicity and prove core Cauchy theorem and integral-formula consequences.
Evaluate real integrals, count zeros and construct elementary conformal maps for planar harmonic potentials.
Construct Taylor and Laurent expansions; calculate contours with residues, singularities and branch choices.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Curves and Surfaces
decks.description: Calculate intrinsic and extrinsic geometry.

includes: Parametrized curves and surfaces, fundamental forms, curvature and geodesics

practice: Calculate geodesics and curvature on an unfamiliar surface and compare two coordinate charts.

outcomes.description: Calculate arclength, Frenet frames, curvature and torsion for regular spatial curves; compare reparametrizations.
Calculate tangent planes, fundamental forms, principal and Gaussian curvature and geodesic equations for parametrized surfaces.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Algebra
decks.description: Use structural algebra across symmetry and arithmetic.

includes: Modules, tensor products, Galois theory, representations and elementary algebraic number theory

practice: Compute a Galois group and character table and analyze factorization in a quadratic integer ring.

outcomes.description: Construct quadratic integer rings; use norms and ideals to explain unique-factorization failure and solve bounded arithmetic examples.
Determine splitting fields and Galois groups; prove finite Galois correspondence and solvability consequences.
Construct modules, tensor products and exact sequences; prove PID structure theorems and universal properties.
Decompose finite-group representations using characters; prove orthogonality and complete reducibility under stated field assumptions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Markov Chains
decks.description: Predict discrete random evolution.

includes: Finite Markov chains, first passage, stationarity and sampling

practice: Implement an absorbing-chain model and independently verify hitting and occupancy results.

outcomes.description: Analyze transition matrices, communicating classes, stationary distributions, hitting probabilities and mean passage times.
Implement categorical and inverse-transform sampling; validate simulated transitions, occupancy and first-passage distributions against calculations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure Theory and Integration
decks.description: Justify integration and measure-based limits.

includes: Measures, measurable functions, Lebesgue integration, product measures and Radon-Nikodym theory

practice: Prove an integral interchange and a change-of-measure result with complete hypotheses.

outcomes.description: Develop Lebesgue integration and Lp inequalities; prove monotone, dominated and Fubini theorems and Radon-Nikodym applications.
Construct measures, measurable functions and product measures; prove extension and almost-everywhere results in standard settings.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Analysis and Evolution
decks.description: Analyze and implement advanced numerical procedures.

includes: Backward error, iterative solvers, FFT and adaptive or stiff ODE integration

practice: Implement spectral and stiff-evolution calculations and document separate rounding and discretization failures.

outcomes.description: Implement iterative linear solvers and FFT; derive convergence criteria and transform complexity and assess spectral approximation error.
Derive forward and backward error bounds and distinguish consistency, stability and convergence in bounded algorithms.
Implement Runge-Kutta, implicit and adaptive ODE methods; analyze stiffness, stability regions and refinement-based error estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Optimization
decks.description: Solve constrained decisions with justified guarantees.

includes: Linear and nonlinear programs, convexity, duality, optimality and algorithms

practice: Implement two allocation solvers and verify primal feasibility, dual bounds and sensitivity.

outcomes.description: Implement gradient, Newton, projected and simplex methods; prove bounded smooth-convex convergence and assess stopping and conditioning.
Derive Lagrange, KKT and LP duality results; prove convex sufficiency and interpret complementary slackness and sensitivity.
Formulate allocation and estimation as linear, convex or nonlinear programs; distinguish feasibility and local or global optima.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Working PDE and Fourier Methods
decks.description: Solve classical spatial and evolving field models.

includes: Classical PDEs, characteristics, Fourier methods, Green functions and boundary conditions

practice: Solve rectangular and spherical boundary problems and verify initial data, boundaries and energy behavior.

outcomes.description: Classify elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic models; specify initial and boundary data and derive characteristic and energy checks.
Solve heat, wave, Laplace and transport equations in one to three dimensions using separation and characteristic coordinates.
Develop Fourier series and transforms, orthogonal eigenfunction expansions and Green functions; check convergence conditions in standard smooth examples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Statistical Inference
decks.description: Estimate effects and validate statistical models.

includes: Likelihood, Bayesian inference, regression, generalized models, design and diagnostics

practice: Implement an estimator and analyze experimental and observational data with model-failure reports.

outcomes.description: Analyze randomized and blocked designs, interactions, missingness and multiplicity; implement resampling and reproducible uncertainty reports.
Derive standard likelihood and conjugate Bayesian estimates, intervals, tests and power; explain coverage and prior sensitivity.
Fit linear and generalized linear models using least squares and derived score-Hessian iteration; diagnose collinearity, residuals and misspecification.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Point-Set Topology
decks.description: Analyze continuous structure without algebraic barriers.

includes: Topological spaces, continuity, compactness, products and quotients

practice: Analyze a quotient space and prove continuity or nonhomeomorphism using topological properties.

outcomes.description: Construct subspace, product and quotient topologies; analyze polygon identifications and maps between surfaces.
Prove continuity, compactness, connectedness and separation properties in metric and nonmetric topological spaces.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics
decks.description: Exploit symmetries and phase-space structure.

includes: Variations, constraints, symmetries, Hamiltonian dynamics and perturbations

practice: Reduce a constrained mechanical system and compare conserved quantities and perturbative trajectories.

outcomes.description: Construct Hamiltonians, Poisson brackets and canonical transformations; solve elementary Hamilton-Jacobi and action-angle problems.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations and holonomic constraints; connect continuous symmetries with conservation laws.
Analyze weak perturbations, small oscillations and elementary chaotic maps or driven systems using stability and phase-space diagnostics.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electricity and Magnetism
decks.description: Calculate electromagnetic fields and responses.

includes: Static fields, materials, circuit transients and Maxwell waves

practice: Solve a field boundary problem and predict a circuit transient with an energy audit.

outcomes.description: Derive capacitance, inductance and RC, RL and RLC responses; reconcile induction and energy balances.
Apply integral and differential Maxwell equations; derive plane waves, polarization, Poynting flux and boundary reflection.
Calculate three-dimensional fields and potentials using sources, symmetry and elementary conductor or dielectric boundaries.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Fluid Mechanics
decks.description: Model continuum motion and transport.

includes: Continuum balances, stress, viscous flow, dimensional analysis and transport

practice: Infer viscosity from channel measurements and compare analytical and supplied numerical flow predictions.

outcomes.description: Derive integral and differential mass, momentum and energy balances and Newtonian stress and Navier-Stokes equations.
Solve hydrostatic, potential, pipe, creeping and elementary boundary-layer flows; calculate dimensionless regimes and similarity scalings.
Formulate advection-diffusion and heat transport; assess turbulence closures and validate provided solvers by conservation and mesh refinement.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Modern Physics
decks.description: Calculate departures from classical physics.

includes: Special relativity, photons, matter waves and bounded atomic models
excludes: General relativity and full quantum mechanics

practice: Compare classical and modern predictions for unfamiliar photon and electron measurements.

outcomes.description: Derive Bohr and one-dimensional standing-wave energy models and identify their physical limitations.
Calculate photoelectric, Compton and matter-wave effects and interpret interference and detection evidence.
Derive Lorentz transformations and apply invariant intervals and energy-momentum to clocks, collisions and lifetimes.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Statistical Physics
decks.description: Derive thermal behavior from microscopic counting.

includes: Ensembles, occupation statistics, fluctuations and phase transitions

practice: Derive an equation of state and susceptibility and compare finite-system and thermodynamic-limit predictions.

outcomes.description: Calculate fluctuations, correlations and response; analyze simple spin models, mean-field transitions and critical-scaling limitations.
Derive microcanonical, canonical and grand-canonical weights and calculate partition-function observables.
Derive classical, Bose and Fermi occupation laws from explicit state-counting rules; calculate gas and oscillator properties.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Animal Behavior
decks.description: Measure behavior and test mechanistic and evolutionary explanations.

includes: Ethograms, learning, communication, foraging, mating and social behavior

practice: Analyze coded behavior and test competing learning or adaptive hypotheses with an ethical study design.

outcomes.description: Compare proximate and ultimate accounts of learning, communication, navigation, mating, cooperation and parental care.
Construct ethograms and focal or scan sampling protocols; measure interobserver agreement and distinguish observation bias from behavioral variation.
Calculate bounded foraging and payoff models; design controlled or comparative tests accounting for ancestry, alternatives and welfare.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Biology
decks.description: Explain spatial cellular mechanisms.

includes: Membranes, organelles, trafficking, cytoskeleton, signaling and cell cycle

practice: Compare trafficking or cell-cycle mechanisms and specify discriminating imaging experiments.

outcomes.description: Explain membrane transport, organelles, targeting, trafficking and cytoskeletal mechanics with spatial and energy-flow representations.
Explain division, adhesion, cell-cycle control and death; distinguish mechanisms using microscopy and intervention time courses.
Trace receptor, messenger and kinase pathways; infer feedback and cross-talk from localization and perturbation evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecological Forecasting and Conservation
decks.description: Forecast ecological change and compare conservation actions.

includes: Structured populations, detection, spatial change and conservation decisions

practice: Develop a detection-aware conservation assessment for a fragmented landscape with stakeholder tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Compare reserves, restoration and harvesting with projections, uncertainty, biodiversity and competing community obligations.
Construct stage matrices and estimate survival, abundance and occupancy using explicitly derived detection likelihoods.
Analyze connectivity, fragmentation and ecosystem budgets using spatial data and bounded dispersal models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Biology
decks.description: Explain and manipulate genetic information.

includes: Information flow, repair, regulation, chromatin and molecular manipulation

practice: Design a gene-regulation experiment from sequence and construct through controls and interpretation.

outcomes.description: Trace replication, repair, transcription, RNA processing and translation with sequence polarity and molecular error control.
Design primers, cloning and editing constructs; interpret sequencing and expression assays with specificity and off-target controls.
Compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic regulation, chromatin and epigenetics using reporter, binding and expression evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Structural Biology
decks.description: Recover and validate macromolecular structure.

includes: Coordinates, diffraction, projection images, restraints and structural validation
excludes: Reconstruction algorithm development and quantum spectroscopy

practice: Reconstruct a bounded model from supplied observations, script geometry checks and report independent validation.

outcomes.description: Develop finite Fourier and projection models; explain phase ambiguity and execute taught crystallographic, cryo-EM or restraint-based reconstruction steps.
Manipulate molecular coordinates; calculate rigid transformations, distances, angles, contacts and least-squares superpositions.
Assess resolution, independent map-model agreement, stereochemistry, cross-validation and heterogeneity; distinguish measured constraints from assumptions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical and Instrumental Chemistry
decks.description: Select and validate instrumental measurements.

includes: Separation, optical and mass analysis, NMR, electroanalysis and validation

practice: Analyze an unknown mixture with complementary detection and a defensible calibration and uncertainty report.

outcomes.description: Explain signal generation and instrument blocks for UV-visible, IR, NMR, mass and electrochemical methods; acquire bounded analytical data.
Select chromatographic and electrophoretic methods; calculate retention, resolution, partition effects and recovery using explicit instrument models.
Design blanks, internal standards and spike recovery; calculate detection limits and assess matrix effects and orthogonal confirmation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms
decks.description: Predict transformations through mechanisms.

includes: Electron flow, substitution, elimination, addition, aromatic and carbonyl chemistry

practice: Predict unfamiliar products and design isotopic or stereochemical tests of competing mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Construct curved-arrow mechanisms using acid-base balance, nucleophilicity and intermediate stability.
Predict substitution, elimination, alkene addition, aromatic substitution and carbonyl pathways under specified conditions.
Explain regio-, stereo- and chemoselectivity and kinetic versus thermodynamic control using competing reaction-coordinate models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Algorithms
decks.description: Prove guarantees for difficult computational problems.

includes: Approximation, randomized, online and streaming algorithms

practice: Prove an approximation or streaming guarantee and construct instances testing its sharpness.

outcomes.description: Design approximation algorithms using relaxations, rounding and primal-dual methods; prove approximation guarantees.
Analyze online and streaming methods using competitive ratios, adversaries and bounded communication or memory lower-bound arguments.
Design randomized algorithms and sketches; prove success and resource bounds using concentration and amplification.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Rendering and Inverse Imaging
decks.description: Derive image formation and inverse estimation.

includes: Radiometric transport, Monte Carlo rendering and inverse imaging

practice: Implement a path tracer and recover bounded scene parameters with bias, variance and ambiguity diagnostics.

outcomes.description: Formulate inverse geometry, reflectance and image-restoration objectives; implement gradients and regularization and assess illumination and structural ambiguity.
Develop radiometry and the rendering equation; derive and implement importance-sampled path tracing with unbiasedness and variance checks.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Cryptographic Theory
decks.description: Prove bounded cryptographic security claims.

includes: Security definitions, reductions, pseudorandomness, encryption, signatures and protocols

practice: Prove a reduction for a toy construction and demonstrate an attack when a crucial condition is removed.

outcomes.description: Derive bounded pseudorandomness, encryption, authentication and signature constructions and analyze their security under explicit assumptions.
Define computational indistinguishability, negligible advantage and security games; construct hybrid and reduction proofs.
Analyze key agreement and elementary commitment or zero-knowledge protocols; identify composition assumptions and construct attacks on weakened variants.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Distributed Systems
decks.description: Build interpretable services under partial failure.

includes: Failure models, consistency, consensus, replication, transactions and observability

practice: Build a replicated store and test consistency during message loss, partitions and crashes.

outcomes.description: Model clocks, causality and asynchronous failure; distinguish consistency models and explain impossibility assumptions.
Design sharding, observability and failure injection; compare availability, latency, consistency and operational complexity.
Implement replicated logs and bounded crash-fault consensus; analyze quorums, partitions, retries and transaction recovery.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Formal Methods and Verification
decks.description: Turn specifications into checkable correctness claims.

includes: Contracts, temporal logic, model checking, SMT and mechanized proofs

practice: Model-check a protocol and mechanize a complementary invariant proof.

outcomes.description: Implement explicit-state reachability and taught SAT/SMT encodings; interpret counterexamples and boundedness limits.
Specify preconditions, postconditions, invariants and temporal safety or liveness with explicit environmental assumptions.
Prove Hoare-logic and refinement claims and encode a bounded proof in an explicitly introduced proof assistant.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Machine Learning
decks.description: Derive and validate learned representations.

includes: Predictive models, latent variables, neural learning and responsible validation

practice: Implement neural and latent models and compare held-out, calibrated and subgroup performance.

outcomes.description: Evaluate calibration, generalization, shift, subgroup errors and privacy; distinguish predictive success from causal or deployment validity.
Derive backpropagation and implement neural networks; implement finite graphical-model elimination and expectation-maximization for specified latent models.
Implement regression, kernels, clustering and principal-component models; select appropriate losses, representations and regularization.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Parallel and High-Performance Computing
decks.description: Implement correct scalable computations.

includes: Parallel models, shared memory, message passing, accelerators and scaling

practice: Parallelize a graph or matrix workload in two execution models and explain scaling limits.

outcomes.description: Implement shared-memory, message-passing and accelerator kernels with explicit synchronization and memory reasoning.
Analyze work, span, speedup and communication; select task, data and pipeline decompositions.
Profile locality, contention, imbalance and transfers; verify equivalence and reproducible scaling.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Security
decks.description: Analyze adversarial failures and engineer defenses.

includes: Threat models, vulnerabilities, applied cryptography, defense and incident judgment

practice: Audit and harden an isolated service and document tested mitigations and responsible disclosure.

outcomes.description: Explain security games and attack probabilities; use authenticated encryption, hashes, signatures and key exchange via audited libraries and explained toy examples.
Harden services, manage secrets and investigate logs; justify least privilege, disclosure, privacy and residual-risk decisions.
Construct threat models and demonstrate memory, injection, authorization and protocol failures in isolated authorized examples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Topology
decks.description: Distinguish spaces using computable algebraic invariants.

includes: Fundamental groups, coverings, chain complexes and homology

practice: Compute fundamental groups and homology of glued spaces and prove a nonexistence claim for a proposed map.

outcomes.description: Construct homotopies and coverings; compute fundamental groups with van Kampen and use lifting arguments to obstruct maps.
Develop chain complexes, boundary matrices, homology and exact sequences; compute simplicial or cellular examples and justify homotopy invariance.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Geometry
decks.description: Calculate geometry independently of coordinates.

includes: Manifolds, tensors, forms, metrics, connections and curvature

practice: Compute curvature and geodesics for a new metric and verify coordinate consistency.

outcomes.description: Calculate Riemann, Ricci and scalar curvature and relate them to parallel transport, deviation and surface topology.
Construct smooth charts, tangent maps, vector fields and differential forms; prove and apply manifold Stokes results in standard settings.
Transform tensors and metrics; derive covariant derivatives, Levi-Civita connections and geodesic equations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Functional Analysis
decks.description: Analyze infinite-dimensional linear structure.

includes: Banach and Hilbert spaces, duality, weak convergence and spectral theory

practice: Prove existence and approximation results for a Hilbert-space inverse problem and diagnose instability.

outcomes.description: Analyze bounded and compact operators; prove compact self-adjoint spectral results and formulate stable or ill-posed inverse problems.
Prove completeness, duality, Hilbert projection and core Banach-space principles; distinguish norm and weak convergence.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Statistical Theory
decks.description: Prove and assess statistical procedures.

includes: Estimator asymptotics, decision theory, efficiency and smoothing

practice: Prove a new estimator's asymptotic distribution and compare finite-sample coverage and risk by simulation.

outcomes.description: Prove consistency and asymptotic normality for bounded estimator families using uniform laws, Taylor expansion and delta methods with regularity conditions.
Compare risk, sufficiency, completeness, efficiency and Bayes or minimax rules; derive representative optimality and lower-bound results.
Derive kernel or series bias-variance behavior and bootstrap validity in standard settings; assess finite-sample departures computationally.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Logic
decks.description: Analyze formal theories and their limitations.

includes: First-order logic, proof systems, model constructions, completeness and incompleteness

practice: Construct a model using compactness and give a precise incompleteness argument with its assumptions.

outcomes.description: Develop arithmetization, diagonal lemmas and representability; derive incompleteness and explain consistency and axiomatic set-theory boundaries.
Define first-order syntax, semantics and derivations; prove soundness and a bounded completeness construction and apply compactness and model arguments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Continuous-Time Stochastic Processes
decks.description: Model continuous-time random systems.

includes: Poisson, continuous-time chains, renewal, queues and event simulation

practice: Build a queue simulator and verify both transient and stationary behavior.

outcomes.description: Construct Poisson and birth-death models; derive generators, forward equations and stationary laws.
Derive elementary renewal and queue performance, including waiting times, stability and renewal-reward calculations.
Implement event-driven simulation and compare transient and stationary estimates with analytical predictions and Monte Carlo uncertainty.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Electrodynamics
decks.description: Solve classical field problems with causality and boundaries.

includes: Green functions, multipoles, radiation, waveguides and covariant fields

practice: Calculate localized-source radiation and verify causal, far-field and energy-conservation limits.

outcomes.description: Solve boundary problems with Green functions, multipoles and waveguide modes; verify uniqueness and boundary conditions.
Develop four-vectors and electromagnetic tensors; derive Lorentz transformations, covariant conservation and gauge relationships.
Derive retarded potentials and calculate dipole and accelerated-charge radiation, scattering and angular energy flux.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astrophysics and Astronomy
decks.description: Infer astronomical properties from physical evidence.

includes: Astronomical observations, radiative transfer, stars, galaxies and planetary systems

practice: Infer an unfamiliar stellar or exoplanet system from calibrated observations and alternative models.

outcomes.description: Calibrate photometry and spectra; infer distance, temperature, velocity and composition using magnitudes, parallax and explained line models.
Derive bounded radiative-transfer and hydrostatic stellar models; explain energy generation, evolution and compact-object limits.
Analyze transit, orbital, galaxy-rotation and population evidence; distinguish selection effects, degeneracy and model disagreement.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Computational Physics
decks.description: Implement validated physical simulations.

includes: Particle integration, Monte Carlo and bounded diffusion discretization

practice: Validate independent dynamical, diffusion and sampling experiments with explicit error budgets.

outcomes.description: Implement pair-force particle dynamics and Verlet stepping with boundaries; compare conservation and timestep dependence.
Implement Monte Carlo integration and Metropolis sampling; derive detailed balance and estimate autocorrelation-adjusted uncertainty.
Derive and implement one-dimensional diffusion finite differences; verify stability, conservation and grid convergence against analytic solutions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Control and System Identification
decks.description: Identify and regulate measured dynamical systems.

includes: State-space models, Laplace transforms, identification, feedback and observers

practice: Identify and control a low-voltage plant with tracking, stability and actuator-limit tests.

outcomes.description: Design PID, pole-placement and observer feedback; assess stability margins, saturation and sampled implementation.
Estimate low-order plant parameters from step and frequency data by least squares; diagnose residuals and unmodeled dynamics.
Develop Laplace transforms and state-space transfer models; calculate poles, frequency response, controllability and observability.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Plasma Foundations
decks.description: Analyze bounded plasma behavior and measurements.

includes: Plasma scales, particle drifts, elementary waves and diagnostics
excludes: Kinetic contour analysis and confinement theory

practice: Analyze supplied discharge diagnostics and calculate scale and drift predictions; physical work requires suitable facilities.

outcomes.description: Interpret taught probe-current and emission models to estimate density or temperature; assess sheath, calibration and diagnostic perturbation limits.
Calculate uniform-field orbits and guiding-center drifts; derive cold-fluid longitudinal waves and identify approximation regimes.
Derive Debye screening, plasma frequency and collision-scale estimates using explicit thermal and charge-displacement models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics
decks.description: Predict quantum measurement and evolution.

includes: States, measurement, wave equations, spin and approximations

practice: Predict spin sequences and bound spectra and compare exact and approximate methods.

outcomes.description: Calculate spin measurements and perturbative, variational and WKB estimates; assess degeneracy and approximation validity.
Construct normalized states and observables; calculate unitary evolution, measurement probabilities, commutators and uncertainty relations.
Solve one-dimensional wells, barriers and oscillators; separate central-potential equations in three-dimensional spherical coordinates and obtain hydrogenic states.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Animal Anatomy and Physiology
decks.description: Explain integrated animal function.

includes: Comparative organ anatomy, transport, homeostasis, coordination and reproduction

practice: Predict integrated exercise, dehydration or temperature responses using anatomy, transport and feedback.

outcomes.description: Explain membrane excitability, neural, muscular and endocrine coordination; interpret organ perturbation time courses.
Explain digestive, metabolic, renal, osmotic and thermal regulation using mass balances and feedback across animal adaptations.
Compare reproductive systems, hormonal cycles and life histories through energetic, regulatory and environmental constraints.
Identify tissues and organ relationships; calculate explained pressure-flow, diffusion and gas-exchange models with physiological assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology
decks.description: Explain emergence of spatial organismal organization.

includes: Fate, pattern, morphogenesis, regeneration and causal developmental evidence

practice: Reconstruct a developmental mechanism and propose a time-resolved discriminating experiment.

outcomes.description: Infer causality from lineage, mosaics, transplantation, timed perturbation and imaging; distinguish fate from survival and timing effects.
Relate division, migration, adhesion, mechanics and death to morphogenesis, stem cells and regeneration.
Explain competence, induction, positional information and gene-regulatory patterning in comparative animal and plant examples.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Graduate Ecological Theory
decks.description: Derive and test ecological dynamics across scales.

includes: Coexistence, food-web stability, spatial dynamics and observation-aware ecological inference

practice: Fit a spatial community model and compare intervention forecasts and coexistence explanations.

outcomes.description: Derive consumer-resource and multispecies models; analyze invasion, coexistence and food-web stability with Jacobians and perturbations.
Develop bounded state-space ecological likelihoods and sequential simulation estimates; compare forecasts while accounting for observation error and nonidentifiability.
Implement spatial patch and stochastic demographic models; compare dispersal, environmental covariance and extinction mechanisms.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Theory
decks.description: Derive and infer population evolutionary processes.

includes: Forward populations, fixation, quantitative genetics, coalescence and historical inference

practice: Implement forward and coalescent models and test competing demographic and selective histories.

outcomes.description: Construct neutral coalescent waiting and branching models; simulate effects of recombination, structure and changing population size.
Infer demographic or selective parameters using bounded likelihoods or summaries; test confounding and historical identifiability.
Derive Wright-Fisher and Moran transitions, fixation, mutation-selection balance and quantitative-genetic response under explicit assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Advanced Experimental Mechanisms
decks.description: Design decisive molecular and cellular investigations.

includes: Mechanistic perturbation, rescue, orthogonal assays and multimodal experimental interpretation

practice: Develop and analyze a mechanistic study combining rescue, temporal evidence and an orthogonal assay.

outcomes.description: Design dose- and time-resolved perturbation, rescue and epistasis experiments that distinguish direct mechanisms from off-target and compensatory effects.
Compare competing mechanistic claims using orthogonal evidence, power, batch effects, reproducibility and ethical alternatives; justify the next decisive experiment.
Explain and integrate binding, fractionation, pulse-chase, quantitative imaging and single-cell assay workflows with controls for abundance and composition.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genomics and Bioinformatics
decks.description: Infer biology from genome-scale evidence.

includes: Alignment, sequence models, assembly, variants, expression and pipeline validation

practice: Implement an alignment engine and complete a reproducible, quality-controlled sequencing analysis.

outcomes.description: Execute and audit read QC, mapping, graph assembly, annotation and variant calling; distinguish algorithm implementation from tool operation.
Analyze expression and sequence relationships with normalization, multiplicity control, phylogenetic uncertainty and biological validation.
Implement alignment dynamic programming and hidden-Markov forward and Viterbi algorithms with defined scoring, transition and emission models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology
decks.description: Explain immune specificity and regulation.

includes: Innate and adaptive immunity, tolerance, memory and immune assays

practice: Analyze an immune dataset and separate cell abundance, specificity and functional activation.

outcomes.description: Explain receptor diversification, antigen presentation, selection, expansion, memory and tolerance using cell-interaction diagrams.
Trace barriers, recognition, complement, inflammation and cytokine recruitment in pathogen control.
Explain and interpret flow gates, antibody and functional assays in infection, vaccination, allergy, autoimmunity and tumor immunity.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology and Virology
decks.description: Identify microbial functions and host interactions.

includes: Microbial and fungal diversity, growth, metabolism, gene transfer and viruses

practice: Characterize safe isolates or supplied infection datasets with identity, growth and susceptibility controls.

outcomes.description: Compare bacterial, archaeal, fungal and protist structures, metabolism, life cycles and ecological roles; combine staining, biochemical and sequence identification.
Measure growth and viable counts; explain nutrient limitation, gene transfer, biofilms and susceptibility assays with appropriate controls.
Compare viral genome, replication and transmission strategies and microbial host interactions; interpret plaque, molecular and resistance evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Biology
decks.description: Connect plant structure and environmental function.

includes: Plant anatomy, life cycles, transport, photosynthesis, growth and stress

practice: Analyze plant water stress using anatomy, gas exchange and growth measurements.

outcomes.description: Explain meristems, hormones, photoperiodism and stress responses; design tests distinguishing growth and signaling mechanisms.
Identify plant tissues and major lineages; compare reproductive structures and alternation of generations.
Calculate explained water-potential and transpiration models; compare xylem, phloem, nutrition and C3, C4 and CAM acquisition.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Quantitative and Systems Biology
decks.description: Construct and test quantitative biological mechanisms.

includes: Reaction networks, stochastic simulation, feedback and dynamic inference

practice: Implement deterministic and stochastic networks and use interventions to challenge mechanism identifiability.

outcomes.description: Develop sensitivity equations and numerical least-squares or likelihood fitting; test identifiability, uncertainty and perturbation-based discrimination.
Translate biochemical diagrams into stoichiometric ODEs; analyze conservation, steady states, feedback and bifurcation examples.
Derive reaction propensities and Gillespie's direct method; implement and compare stochastic distributions with deterministic trajectories.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry
decks.description: Explain chemical fate and compare interventions.

includes: Environmental speciation, reaction-exchange models, atmospheric and aquatic chemistry and risk judgment

practice: Analyze contamination with speciation and compartment calculations, sampling and an intervention comparison.

outcomes.description: Design sampling and compare remediation through effectiveness, uncertainty, exposure, ecological burden and environmental-justice consequences.
Construct compartment balances with partitioning, first-order reaction and exchange; solve bounded scalar or steady algebraic models for persistence and exposure.
Explain atmospheric photochemistry, aquatic carbonate and redox systems and soil sorption using chemical mechanisms and evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Materials and Polymer Chemistry
decks.description: Choose processing and characterization for material properties.

includes: Polymerization, material synthesis, diffraction, interfaces and energy materials using bounded models
excludes: General polymer thermodynamics and industrial qualification

practice: Design synthesis and complementary characterization for a specified polymer or electrode and reconcile measured properties.

outcomes.description: Apply explained adsorption isotherms, colloidal force-balance models and charge bookkeeping to surfaces and electrochemical energy materials.
Select crystalline, amorphous and nanoscale synthesis routes; interpret Bragg diffraction, thermal transitions and imaging using explicit structural models.
Compare chain and step growth; derive conversion and molecular-weight measures from finite distributions and relate architecture to thermal and mechanical observations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry
decks.description: Derive approximate molecular energies and spectra.

includes: Electronic Hamiltonians, antisymmetry, molecular approximation and transitions

practice: Construct a bounded variational calculation and predict molecular transitions with an approximation audit.

outcomes.description: Construct electronic Hamiltonians, antisymmetrized states and variational matrices; derive Hartree-Fock equations and their limitations.
Apply Born-Oppenheimer separation and symmetry to bonding, potential surfaces, rotations and harmonic vibrations.
Calculate transition moments, selection rules and rotational, vibrational and electronic spacings from approximate molecular states.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Structure Elucidation
decks.description: Infer complex molecular structures from working spectra.

includes: Multinuclear and two-dimensional NMR, mass fragmentation, stereochemical and exchange assignments

practice: Solve an unknown structure from raw one- and two-dimensional spectra and defend alternative-assignment tests.

outcomes.description: Explain and interpret carbon NMR, COSY, HSQC, HMBC and NOE correlation rules, acquisition controls and ambiguities; combine them with mass fragmentation.
Resolve connectivity, relative stereochemistry, conformer populations and bounded exchange behavior using complementary spectra and explicit slow/fast-exchange models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Synthesis
decks.description: Plan practical multistep syntheses.

includes: Retrosynthesis, carbon-carbon formation, redox, pericyclic models and execution

practice: Design and, when authorized, execute a short synthesis with intermediate identification and route comparison.

outcomes.description: Plan reagents, workups, purification and structural checkpoints; calculate cumulative yield and compare hazard, waste and scalability.
Apply enolate, organometallic, redox and elementary pericyclic methods with explicit selectivity and orbital-symmetry models.
Plan disconnections, functional-group conversions, protecting groups and convergent alternatives for unfamiliar targets.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Machine Learning
decks.description: Develop probabilistic and sequential learners.

includes: Generalization, generative modeling, sequences and reinforcement learning

practice: Derive and implement generative and sequential objectives and compare against transparent baselines.

outcomes.description: Prove finite-class generalization and bounded stability results; analyze regularization, optimization bias and representation assumptions.
Derive variational bounds and implement latent generative and attention-based sequence models with explicit likelihood and sampling procedures.
Derive Bellman equations and implement dynamic programming, temporal differences and policy gradients; assess exploration, off-policy bias and reward misspecification.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Robotics
decks.description: Integrate geometry, inference and control.

includes: Robot geometry, localization, mapping, planning and control integration

practice: Build a simulated localization-planning-control stack and quantify sensor and actuator failures.

outcomes.description: Derive and implement Kalman and particle localization with explicit motion and sensor likelihoods; analyze observability and map uncertainty.
Construct rigid transformations, forward and inverse kinematics and Jacobians, developing needed partial derivatives locally; identify singularities.
Implement configuration-space collision checking, sampling-based planning and feedback tracking; assess actuator, uncertainty and safety limits.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Probability and Stochastic Calculus
decks.description: Analyze random limits and continuous stochastic evolution.

includes: Conditional expectation, martingales, Brownian motion, Ito calculus and diffusion simulation

practice: Derive and simulate diffusion observables and justify every stopping and limiting step.

outcomes.description: Construct conditional expectation through Radon-Nikodym theory; prove convergence-mode relations and standard probabilistic limit results.
Construct Ito integration and derive Ito's formula; solve elementary SDEs and connect generators, forward equations and Euler-Maruyama refinement.
Prove bounded martingale convergence and stopping results; develop Brownian properties from Gaussian increments with explicit hypotheses.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Partial Differential Equations
decks.description: Analyze weak PDE solutions and numerical approximations.

includes: Well-posedness, Sobolev formulations, energy estimates and convergent discretization

practice: Prove an energy estimate and implement a convergent two-dimensional boundary solver.

outcomes.description: Prove representative uniqueness, stability and regularity estimates for elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic initial-boundary problems.
Implement finite differences and piecewise-linear finite elements; establish consistency, coercivity or stability and convergence bounds.
Construct distributional derivatives and Sobolev spaces; derive weak formulations and prove bounded variational existence and energy results.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Quantum Theory
decks.description: Calculate interacting quantum processes.

includes: Symmetries, scattering, mixed states, second quantization and path integrals

practice: Calculate transitions and scattering and compare first- and second-quantized descriptions.

outcomes.description: Construct bosonic and fermionic Fock spaces and Hamiltonians; derive elementary path-integral and many-body mean-field descriptions.
Derive time-dependent rates, Born and partial-wave scattering and resolvent formulations with controlled approximations.
Construct rotation representations and coupled angular momenta; apply selection rules and analyze density operators and partial traces.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Nonequilibrium Statistical Mechanics
decks.description: Connect microscopic dynamics with relaxation and transport.

includes: Kinetic equations, relaxation, stochastic response, entropy production and critical scaling

practice: Compare kinetic and stochastic relaxation models against correlation data and verify entropy and transport predictions.

outcomes.description: Analyze coarse-graining and elementary renormalization recursions for critical equilibrium and relaxation scaling; identify finite-size and mean-field limits.
Derive Boltzmann collision and relaxation-time models; calculate transport coefficients and analyze conservation and entropy-production assumptions.
Develop Langevin and Fokker-Planck models and fluctuation-dissipation relations; calculate correlations and linear response in bounded systems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
decks.description: Interpret nuclear and particle evidence.

includes: Nuclear models, decay, reactions, particles and detectors

practice: Analyze decay or scattering data and compare hypotheses after detector corrections.

outcomes.description: Explain ionization, scintillation and semiconductor detection; infer lifetimes and cross sections with efficiency, background and counting corrections.
Calculate binding energies, decay chains and thresholds; compare nuclear models, fission, fusion and scattering evidence.
Classify particles and interactions; apply symmetry, conservation and relativistic kinematics to reaction channels.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Graduate Plasma Physics
decks.description: Analyze fluid and kinetic plasma limits.

includes: Two-fluid and MHD equations, kinetic dispersion and plasma stability

practice: Calculate a magnetized plasma spectrum and explain fluid failures and confinement instabilities.

outcomes.description: Derive two-fluid and MHD equations; analyze bounded magnetized equilibria and wave modes.
Formulate Vlasov dynamics and derive dispersion and Landau damping using an explicit causal contour prescription.
Derive representative fluid and kinetic instability criteria and compare confinement and damping predictions across regimes.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity and Cosmology
decks.description: Connect spacetime geometry with observable gravitation.

includes: Einstein equations, spacetime observables and cosmological evolution

practice: Calculate a relativistic observable and compare bounded cosmological models with supplied data.

outcomes.description: Derive Friedmann evolution and distance-redshift relations; compare expansion, background radiation and structure evidence with parameter degeneracies.
Construct stress-energy tensors and Einstein equations; derive conservation structure and the Newtonian weak-field limit.
